source.title: HiPACE: Hierarchical Phase-Boundary Analysis and Controlled Evaluation of Feature Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Jin-Yuan Zhang; Peng-Ji He; Yin Yuan; He-Long Hu; Sheng-Shuo Jiao

page_placements.theme: Hierarchical absorption, hedging and sparse-coding optima

record.tranche_reason: Tests hierarchical feature-absorption thresholds and their structural consequences using a different generator, SAE evaluation, and measures from Toy Models of Superposition; it does not reproduce that paper’s method.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s synthetic phase-boundary tests, reported SAE structural and proxy measurements, controlled activation composition, and residual-stream interventions. The paper also cites prior results and gives theory and metric-selection details; cited results and values used only to select or define analyses are not recorded as findings.
record.test_reason: The study is mainly a theory and evaluation of SAE feature absorption, not of superposition in networks. Its real-SAE results bear on V5: Pythia-160m TopK SAE dictionaries allocate shared parent–child family directions in line with a sparsity-cost ordering, and parent and child directions have equal causal effects, so the effect sits in a family subspace rather than a unique atom. Its synthetic phase boundary concerns an SAE's L0 coding trade-off on a hierarchical generator with fewer features than dimensions. It does not test toy-model superposition (V1).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. Authors also state that the preregistered instance-level proxy was falsified (ρ = +0.41, wrong direction). They call this a metric-mediated non-transfer, attributed mainly to the 1/K baseline, with transfer under a corrected metric left open. They note that layer dependence cautions against treating a single decoder atom as canonical.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a hierarchical Bernoulli parent-plus-residual generator, an L0 cost comparison, family-level WordNet SAE measurements, and controlled activation/intervention tests rather than reproducing the original Toy Models of Superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The structural outcome depends on layer and statistic: the paper reports stronger results at L6 and L11, weaker at L9, and no formed signal at L3; the preregistered singleton proxy gives different results across estimator, layer, and hook.

fits_no_version.finding: Closed-form L0 phase boundary at which an SAE prefers a single parent atom over child atoms. It matches exact synthetic onsets on 30/30 cells and trained TopK SAEs on 12/16 cells.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature absorption of hierarchical features follows a sparsity-penalty phase boundary λc = α²k/(k−1).

fits_no_version.finding: Parent-direction SAE activation rises with the number of composed active children (ρ = +0.85 to +0.96).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE parent latents respond to the count of active child concepts, as absorption theory predicts.

fits_no_version.finding: The preregistered instance-level absorption proxy fails in the wrong direction (ρ = +0.41 at 160m, +0.49 at 410m), driven by a 1/K family-size baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Absorption-threshold predictions transfer to real SAE top-1 firing.

record.problems: The real structural pipeline is tested primarily on one model (Pythia-160m) and one public SAE family. The authors report that randomized siblings and family-size control do not jointly match token frequency, decoder norm, hierarchy depth, and lexical similarity. The preregistered proxy fails, and a corrected proxy remains open. Causal evidence comes from controlled perturbations; necessity during natural prompting is not tested. Some supplementary outcomes are given only in figure captions.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: No network storing more sparse features than dimensions. The synthetic phase boundary is an SAE sparsity-penalty trade-off, not a feature-sparsity transition, and there is no geometry test.
Neuron polysemanticity and capacity allocation are not studied.
Assumes SAEs recover sparse features. It does not test spread across neurons or recoverability itself.
Completeness and stability across independently trained dictionaries or models are not tested. Only one SAE family on Pythia-160m is used.
Assumes 1-D parent and child directions. Feature dimensionality is not measured.

missing.what: Structural decoder-gap results at L3 (not formed) and L9 (weaker). These are stated only qualitatively, with values in Figure 7. The layer dependence bears on whether atoms are canonical across layers.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked the synthetic SAE phase boundary to V1, but it is a different construct: SAE dictionary allocation under an L0 penalty, not superposition in a network. The V5 verdict rests on interpretation of absorption structure and the equal parent/child intervention effects. The study tests one SAE family and does not test V5's stability or completeness.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the original toy-model geometry or its regular geometric configurations directly. The synthetic generator assumes orthogonal child residuals; the real-model tests use WordNet family statistics and one primary model/SAE family.
Does not test neuron polysemanticity, the allocation of dedicated dimensions to important features, or feature importance.
Does not test whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.
Tests SAE-recovered family structure in Pythia-160m and reports a proxy replication on Pythia-410m, but does not test feature spread across many neurons or broad model coverage.
Interventions compare family directions, but do not establish feature completeness or stability across independently trained dictionaries or models.
The paper tests effects of parent and child directions, not the dimensionality or geometry of the underlying representation as a direct coding measurement.

rows.subject: hierarchical Bernoulli generator
rows.operation_detail: Compared exact parent-absorption and child-coding costs and measured the 50% absorption onset.
rows.measure: Relative error of observed onset versus λc(k⋆, α)
rows.value: Observed onset agrees within ±15% on all 30/30 cells; median absolute relative error 0.026; maximum 0.053; 900 runs
rows.note: The result is for the paper’s hierarchical generator and its stated assumptions.
rows.check: Measures when an L0-penalised dictionary prefers parent absorption over child coding. λ is the SAE's sparsity penalty, not feature sparsity, and K+1 ≤ d=64, so there is no superposition. Not V1.

rows.subject: trained TopK SAEs
rows.operation_detail: Compared trained SAE crossover with the predicted boundary.
rows.value: Recovered within one budget in 12 of 16 cells
rows.note: The paper says the four deviations occur at K = 16, where dictionaries retain a parent atom alongside child residuals.
rows.check: Trained TopK SAE crossover on the synthetic generator. This is the SAE coding regime, not a network storing more features than dimensions. Not V1.

rows.subject: trained TopK SAEs
rows.operation_detail: Examined the deviations from the predicted crossover.
rows.measure: Crossover relative to the pure-strategy boundary
rows.value: Four deviations; dictionaries retain a parent atom alongside child residuals, in the mixed regime
rows.note: The authors interpret these as mixed-strategy cases rather than a failure of the boundary’s pure-strategy comparison.
rows.check: Restates the 4 deviating cells already counted in R2, so it is not a separate result. Not V1.

source_check.problem: Describes the four exceptions already counted in R2; do not count it as independent evidence.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: Pythia-160m, EleutherAI TopK SAE, residual L6/L11, WordNet noun families
labels.reason: The combined results and explicit discussion qualify attribution to a unique parent atom: structural recovery is layer-dependent and parent/child interventions have equal median effects. This is a granularity qualification, not evidence that completeness, stability, or canonicality is absent.

relation.reason: Its own structural and intervention results bear on the scope of V5, although they do not directly establish or disprove canonicality.

tranche.reason: The study gives a specific argument qualifying unique-atom interpretations of SAE representations, supported by layer-dependent family structure and comparable parent/child intervention effects.

source_check.notes: R1's untruncated median absolute relative error is 0.026; maximum 0.053. The structural endpoint was developed after the preregistered proxy failed; the subsequent holdout was frozen, and interventions establish sufficiency rather than natural-prompt necessity.

statements.correction: Pythia-160m residual L6; strength 1.0; parent-signed and child-signed injections each yield +0.0523 median true-parent logit-margin shift. Family-subspace causal sufficiency; unique-atom attribution unresolved. V5 implication: limits_scope.
statements.problem: The Pythia numerical claim is correct, but a challenges label overstates this study's evidence. It does not demonstrate individual-atom variation or absence of canonical units.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
